Elaine (PM): Design review for Alerting & SLO config UI prototype: https://figma.com/file/xyz-alerting-slo (please focus on thresholds, notification preview, and suppression UX) :eyes: Marco (Product Designer): Quick notes: main goal is make thresholds readable at a glance. thinking compact cards per rule, left column SLO/metric, middle column threshold + duration, right column channels + preview button. mock attached. :thumbsup: Sam (Frontend): I like cards. accessibility nit: ensure the threshold inputs have explicit labels and numeric keyboard support. sliders are nice but must degrade to text input. also need aria-live on the preview area so screen readers get updates when you click "Preview". Marco (Product Designer): Agreed. For copy, instead of "Threshold value" use "Trigger when" e.g., "Trigger when error rate > 5% for 5 minutes" it's more natural. Also propose an inline humanized preview sentence under the inputs. Jess (SRE): Two operational points: (1) suppression windows should default to 5 minutes and be easy to set to 'instance'/'route'/'global'. (2) Notification channels list needs last-tested timestamp and a lightweight "test channel" flow. Don't want to accidentally spam all channels on preview. Elaine (PM): On suppression placement Marco put it under the advanced panel, but I think it should sit next to channels (so you can pick channel + suppression scope together). That reduces cognitive load when deciding where to mute. Sam (Frontend): UX for preview: don't send real notifications by default. The preview should show a rendered sample (email, slack, pagerduty) plus an optional checkbox "Send live test to selected channels". Also debounce the preview calls we will be hitting the render service a lot. Marco (Product Designer): Good: add a small inline "Payload preview" toggle. When toggled on it shows a read-only JSON and a rendered view. Example copy on the toggle: "Preview notification payload (no live sends)". Jess (SRE): For channels, list order should be weighted by type (pagerduty first, slack next, then email). Also let users pin a fallback channel that gets notified if the primary fails. Sam (Frontend): Accessibility code sketch for the preview pane: ```html
...rendered payload...
``` Keep keyboard trap free inside the modal and ensure Escape closes preview. Marco (Product Designer): Copy tweak: change button "Run preview" -> "Preview notification" and secondary action "Send test" (with confirmation). Also change "Suppression" label to "Mute for" to match common parlance. Elaine (PM): Questions for devs: can we include a "What would trigger this" inline explanation that shows an example timeline? e.g., small sparkline + text "Failed 6 times in 10m -> triggered". That helps non-SRE PMs understand the window. Jess (SRE): We can provide a synthetic timeline from recent metrics but warn about sampling. Also: include a "noise risk" estimate (low/medium/high) based on history. That could be a visual pill next to the threshold. Sam (Frontend): Implementation note: the "Mute for" dropdown should accept minutes, hours, and a custom cron-like suppression window (for advanced users). Keep default presets: 5m, 30m, 1h, 24h. We'll need API changes to accept suppression scope: rule, service, environment. Marco (Product Designer): Visual accessibility: use >=3:1 contrast for the small pills (noise risk, last-tested). If we use color to indicate severity, also include an icon and accessible text so color isn't the only cue. Elaine (PM): UX decision: inline vs modal for channel selection lean inline expanded list to avoid context switch. But keep a compact modal for "Configure advanced integration settings" for PD/email templates. Any objections? Jess (SRE): Inline is fine. For PagerDuty we need to show the integration routing key and last successful delivery. Also an opt-out toggle "Don't notify during maintenance windows". Sam (Frontend): Small interaction detail: when user edits threshold duration, update the humanized sentence live and show a small tooltip with the raw rule expression (e.g., "sum(rate(errors[5m])) / sum(rate(reqs[5m])) > 0.05 for 5m"). That helps power users. Marco (Product Designer): Final checklist for the next mock: 1) wireframes with suppression next to channels, 2) preview toggle + rendered + raw JSON, 3) humanized sentence + raw expression tooltip, 4) noise-risk pill, 5) accessibility annotations (aria labels, focus order), 6) copy swaps (Trigger when / Preview notification / Send test / Mute for). Elaine (PM): I'll consolidate and send an updated Figma by EOD. Thanks all please add any edge cases here. :sparkles: notify-bot: Reminder: design-review scheduled in #design tomorrow 10:00am. Link: https://calendar.redwood.ai/event/12345 Marco (Product Designer): One edge case overlapping rules: we should show when a rule is shadowed by a higher-priority rule and offer a "View overlapping rules" quick link. Jess (SRE): Also: rate-limit previews per user (e.g., 1/sec) to protect render service. Sam (Frontend): I'll file a small tech-debt ticket for the debounce + rate-limit. Elaine (PM): Perfect. Closing this thread after Figma update. :white_check_mark:
